entries.answer:
I want to upgrade the existing Base64 × 805 text encoder and decoder into a complete, productionready web application so that users can reliably encode UTF8 text by multiplying every byte value by 805 before Base64 serialization, decode only valid Base64 × 805 payloads back to their exact original text, copy results, receive clear validation feedback, and use the interface on desktop and mobile devices.

Construct the full upgrade as exactly two source files:

1. A single backend file containing all serverside behavior, configuration, API endpoints, validation logic, staticfile serving, security headers, error handling, and startup logic.
2. A single index.html file containing the entire frontend application, including all styles, SVG icons, JavaScript behavior, responsive layout rules, modal or secondary views if required, and every userfacing screen. Do not create separate CSS, JavaScript, component, asset, route, page, configuration, or helper files. Do not use placeholders, simulated behavior, mock data, dummy data, fake API responses, unfinished functions, or abbreviated code. Provide complete, unabridged, executable productionready code for both files.

Use Node.js with Express in one backend file named server.js. Use only dependencies that are explicitly declared and necessary. The backend must serve index.html from the same project directory, expose a health endpoint, expose encoding and decoding API endpoints, validate every request fully, return structured JSON responses, and never trust clientside validation alone.

Implement the backend requirements in this order:

1. Initialize an Express application.
2. Enable JSON request parsing with a conservative request body size limit suitable for text conversion, such as 1 MB.
3. Set secure HTTP response headers without breaking sameorigin frontend functionality:
    X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
    X-Frame-Options: DENY
    Referrer-Policy: no-referrer
    A restrictive Content Security Policy that permits only sameorigin scripts and styles embedded in index.html; do not allow external resource loading.
4. Disable Express fingerprinting with app.disable("x-powered-by").
5. Serve the single index.html file from the project root.
6. Add GET /api/health, returning JSON with an ok: true property.
7. Add POST /api/encode.
8. Add POST /api/decode.
9. Add centralized error handling for invalid JSON, oversized payloads, malformed input, and unexpected server errors. Never expose stack traces or internal implementation details in API responses.
10. Start the server using PORT from the environment, falling back to port 3000.

Define the encoding contract precisely:

 The request body for POST /api/encode must be JSON in this exact shape:

json
{
  "text": "..."
}


 Reject a request when text is missing, is not a string, or exceeds 100,000 UTF16 JavaScript code units.
 Permit an empty string and encode it successfully.
 Convert the text into UTF8 bytes using TextEncoder.
 For every input byte \(b\), calculate \(m = b \times 805\).
 Since \(0 \le b \le 255\), the multiplied number is in the range \(0\) through \(205275\), which fits safely inside an unsigned 32bit integer.
 Store each multiplied number as exactly four bytes in bigendian order.
 Concatenate all fourbyte values into one binary payload.
 Convert the binary payload to a standard Base64 string.
 Return this exact successful response shape:

json
{
  "ok": true,
  "result": "BASE64_RESULT",
  "inputCharacters": 0,
  "inputBytes": 0,
  "outputCharacters": 0
}


 Set inputCharacters to text.length.
 Set inputBytes to the UTF8 byte length.
 Set outputCharacters to the Base64 result length.
 Do not add timestamps, random values, encryption keys, reversible secrets, or nondeterministic output.

Define the decoding contract precisely:

 The request body for POST /api/decode must be JSON in this exact shape:

json
{
  "encoded": "..."
}


 Reject a request when encoded is missing, is not a string, or exceeds 600,000 characters.
 Remove only leading and trailing whitespace with trim(). Do not remove whitespace inside the Base64 string.
 Permit an empty string and decode it successfully to an empty text string.
 Validate Base64 strictly before decoding:
   Its length must be divisible by four, except the empty string.
   It may contain only A–Z, a–z, 0–9, +, /, and zero to two trailing = padding characters.
   Padding may appear only at the end.
   Reject invalid Base64 rather than attempting recovery.
 Decode the Base64 text into bytes.
 Reject the input if the decoded byte count is not divisible by four.
 Read every fourbyte group as an unsigned 32bit bigendian integer \(m\).
 Reject the payload when \(m \bmod 805 \ne 0\).
 Calculate \(b = m / 805\).
 Reject the payload when \(b\) is outside the inclusive range 0 through 255.
 Build the original byte array from each validated byte value.
 Decode the byte array as UTF8 using TextDecoder with fatal: true; reject invalid UTF8 rather than replacing invalid bytes.
 Return this exact successful response shape:

json
{
  "ok": true,
  "result": "ORIGINAL_TEXT",
  "inputCharacters": 0,
  "inputBytes": 0,
  "outputCharacters": 0
}


 Set inputCharacters to the trimmed Base64 input length.
 Set inputBytes to the decoded binary payload length.
 Set outputCharacters to the decoded text length.
 Return client errors as HTTP 400 with this exact structure:

json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": "Human-readable validation message"
}


 Return unexpected server failures as HTTP 500 with the same response shape but a generic safe error message.

Implement the frontend entirely inside index.html. Use no external fonts, CSS libraries, JavaScript libraries, frameworks, CDN files, images, icon packages, analytics, trackers, or thirdparty network requests. Use semantic HTML, accessible labels, keyboardoperable controls, inline SVG icons, native browser APIs, and vanilla JavaScript. The frontend must call the backend API using fetch with sameorigin relative paths only.

Create a singlepage application with three fully implemented views rendered in the same index.html file:

1. The Converter view.
2. The Method view.
3. The Privacy view.

Do not implement separate HTML files or clientside URL routes. Use a compact header navigation that switches visible views through JavaScript and updates the active navigation state. Preserve the user’s converter text, encoded text, output, selected direction, and recent activity while switching views.

Apply this exact visual system as CSS custom properties in :root:

css
:root {
  --bg: #000000;
  --surface-deep: #09090f;
  --fg: #f5f5f7;
  --fg-72: rgba(246, 255, 249, 0.72);
  --fg-60: rgba(245, 245, 247, 0.60);
  --fg-45: rgba(245, 245, 247, 0.45);
  --fg-25: rgba(245, 245, 247, 0.25);
  --white: #ffffff;
  --blue: #0000ff;
  --accent: #0000ff;
  --separator: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.16);
  --surface-card: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.055);
  --surface-card-hover: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.085);
  --surface-input: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.065);
  --surface-input-focus: rgba(0, 0, 255, 0.13);
  --danger: #ff5b5b;
  --success: #78f0ae;
  --radius-bubble: 18px;
  --radius-card: 16px;
  --radius-pill: 23px;
  --radius-circle: 50%;
  --space-xs: 2px;
  --space-sm-1: 3px;
  --space-sm-2: 4px;
  --space-sm-3: 5px;
  --space-sm-4: 6px;
  --space-sm-5: 7px;
  --space-1: 8px;
  --space-2: 10px;
  --space-3: 11px;
  --space-4: 12px;
  --space-5: 13px;
  --space-6: 14px;
  --space-md: 16px;
  --space-md-2: 17px;
  --space-lg: 20px;
}


Apply this typography system exactly:

 Use -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif as the complete system font stack.
 Default body text: 16px, 400 weight.
 Medium UI text: 16px, 500 weight.
 Semibold UI text: 16px, 600 weight.
 Caption text: 11px, 400 weight.
 Caption semibold metadata: 11px, 600 weight, 0.5px letter spacing.
 Subheadings: 15px, 600 weight, 0.3px letter spacing.
 Longform content and output text: 16px, 400 weight, 23.2px lineheight.

Construct the app shell as follows:

 Use a fullheight black background.
 Create a centered application shell with a maximum width of 980px.
 Apply horizontal page padding of 20px on desktop and 14px on mobile.
 Use a deep navyblack header gradient that transitions from --surface-deep into --bg.
 Keep the header visible at the top during normal page scrolling without using a fixed overlay that obscures content.
 Display a small inline SVG mark at the left of the product name.
 Use the product title Base64 × 805.
 Add the subtitle Deterministic UTF-8 byte transformation.
 Include navigation buttons labeled Converter, Method, and Privacy.
 Give the active navigation item a blue accent indicator and clear aria-current="page" state.
 On narrow screens, retain usable navigation by allowing horizontal navigation scrolling instead of clipping or collapsing controls invisibly.

Construct the Converter view as the primary view:

 Show an eyebrow label reading TEXT TRANSFORMATION.
 Show the title Encode and decode with Base64 × 805.
 Show a concise description explaining that every UTF8 byte is multiplied by 805, serialized as a fourbyte bigendian integer, and Base64 encoded.
 Include a segmented direction selector with two controls:
   Encode text
   Decode payload
 The selector must be accessible as a radio group or equivalent keyboardoperable selection mechanism.
 When Encode text is selected:
   Show the input label Plain text.
   Show an editable textarea with a useful, nonplaceholderonly accessible label.
   Use the actual text Enter UTF-8 text to transform as the textarea placeholder.
   Disable browser spellcheck for the input field.
   Show a byte and character counter that accurately recalculates for Unicode content using TextEncoder.
   Show the primary action button text Encode to Base64.
   Display the output label Encoded payload.
 When Decode payload is selected:
   Show the input label Base64 × 805 payload.
   Show the actual text Paste a Base64 × 805 payload to restore its text as the textarea placeholder.
   Disable browser spellcheck for the input field.
   Show a character counter and decoded binary byte estimate only when strict Base64 structure permits an estimate.
   Show the primary action button text Decode to text.
   Display the output label Decoded text.
 Preserve separate draft values for the encoding and decoding modes. Switching modes must not overwrite either draft.
 Include a Clear button that clears only the current mode’s input, current mode’s result, validation message, and corresponding counters, without touching the other mode.
 Include a swapdirection button represented by an inline SVG icon and accessible name Use output as input in the opposite direction.
 Enable the swapdirection button only when the current output exists:
   If currently encoding, switch to decoding and put the encoded output into the decoding input.
   If currently decoding, switch to encoding and put the decoded output into the plaintext input.
 Do not silently trim or modify a plaintext encoding input.
 On decode, the displayed input state may retain the userentered text while the backend applies only leading and trailing trimming according to the API contract.
 Use a results textarea or preformatted output area that preserves line breaks, supports text selection, and has a clear accessible name.
 Make the output readonly but selectable.
 Add a copy button with an inline SVG copy icon and accessible name Copy output.
 Disable the copy button when output is empty.
 After a successful copy, show a nonblocking success message such as Copied to clipboard and change the copy icon state briefly. Restore the normal state automatically after approximately two seconds.
 Handle clipboard permission or browser failures by showing a clear nonblocking error message and retaining the output.
 Show an inline live status region for loading, success, validation errors, API errors, and clipboard errors. Use aria-live="polite" for normal completion and status updates; use role="alert" for errors.
 Disable action controls while a request is in progress and show a visible loading state such as Encoding… or Decoding….
 Prevent duplicate requests while processing.
 Submit from the keyboard with Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter while focus is in the input textarea.
 On successful transformations, display precise metadata:
   For encoding: plaintext character count, UTF8 byte count, and Base64 output character count.
   For decoding: trimmed Base64 character count, decoded binary byte count, and decoded text character count.
 Keep the most recent successful result visible until the user clears it, replaces it through another successful request, or swaps it into the opposite input.
 If a transformation fails, preserve both the current input and the previous successful output. Do not erase the result because a subsequent request fails.

Add a compact recentactivity panel below the converter:

 Store up to five most recent successful transformations in browser localStorage.
 Store only operation type, input character count, input byte count, output character count, and a local timestamp.
 Never store source text, decoded text, encoded values, or any transformation payload in localStorage.
 Render each entry with its type, counts, and local timestamp.
 Add a Clear activity control that removes only the local activity metadata.
 If localStorage is unavailable or throws an exception, keep the converter fully usable and display a nonblocking message that activity cannot be saved locally.
 Do not claim that the application has persisted or deleted data unless the operation actually succeeded.

Construct the Method view with fully written technical content. Include all of the following exact concepts:

 It is a deterministic reversible byte transformation, not encryption.
 Text is encoded into UTF8 bytes.
 Each byte \(b\) is transformed into \(b \times 805\).
 Each transformed value is stored as an unsigned 32bit bigendian integer.
 The resulting binary data is serialized with standard Base64.
 Decoding reverses the process by strict Base64 validation, reading fourbyte values, checking divisibility by 805, enforcing the byte range 0–255, and fatal UTF8 decoding.
 Explain the concrete example that the UTF8 byte value 65 for the character A becomes \(65 \times 805 = 52325\), then returns to 65 during decoding.
 State clearly that Base64 is an encoding format and does not provide secrecy, authentication, integrity protection, or cryptographic security.
 State that the backend rejects malformed payloads rather than attempting to repair them.
 Present the encoding and decoding process as ordered steps and include the exact mathematical notation using escaped HTML entities or readable text.

Construct the Privacy view with fully written, accurate behaviorspecific content. Do not make broad unsupported privacy claims. State all of the following:

 The converter submits input to the sameorigin backend API for transformation.
 The backend processes the request in memory to create the response and does not implement persistent storage in this application.
 The browser may store only recentactivity metadata locally when localStorage is available.
 Recentactivity metadata contains operation type, input character count, input byte count, output character count, and a local timestamp.
 Recentactivity metadata does not contain plain text, decoded text, encoded payloads, or transformation results.
 Clipboard copying occurs only after the user presses the copy control.
 Network, browser extensions, reverse proxies, hosting providers, deployment logging, and browser settings can affect privacy outside the application code; do not promise protection from those systems.
 Advise users not to process sensitive secrets unless they control and trust the deployment environment.

Implement the frontend interaction model in detail:

 Maintain a single application state object containing:
   Active view.
   Active converter direction.
   Plaintext input draft.
   Encodedpayload input draft.
   Output value.
   Output metadata.
   Request loading state.
   Status message and status type.
   Recent activity metadata.
 Render all mutable interface state from this state object rather than allowing mode switches to lose unsynchronized values.
 Attach event listeners after the DOM loads.
 Use TextEncoder for clientside UTF8 byte counting.
 Implement a strict clientside Base64 structural checker only for displaying the decode byte estimate; backend validation remains authoritative.
 Use fetch("/api/encode", ...) and fetch("/api/decode", ...) with Content-Type: application/json.
 Parse JSON only after verifying a JSON response when practical; gracefully handle nonJSON server or network errors.
 Treat non2xx responses as errors even if the response body is malformed.
 Add a request timeout using AbortController; use a realistic timeout such as 15 seconds.
 Cancel and clean up timers and abort handlers correctly after every completed request.
 Do not use innerHTML to insert user input, output, status text, activity values, or server messages. Use textContent, DOM property assignment, or carefully constructed static HTML.
 If any static rich text must be inserted dynamically, define it as static constants under application control only.
 Protect against UI exceptions by validating DOM references and wrapping fallible browser storage and clipboard calls in error handling.
 Make every control operable with keyboard navigation.
 Ensure visible focus states meet high contrast requirements.
 Respect prefers-reduced-motion by removing or significantly reducing transitions and animations.
 Prevent horizontal page overflow at all supported viewport widths.
 Support narrow viewports from 320px upward and desktop layouts up to the maximum shell width.
 Use an accessible contrast ratio for all text, controls, borders, active states, errors, and disabled states against the black or darksurface backgrounds.
 Do not use gradients other than the deep navyblack header background.
 Do not use decorative imagery.

Implement the visual layout in this order:

1. Header with brand and navigation.
2. Main content area with all three views.
3. Converter hero and controls.
4. Input/output conversion card.
5. Recentactivity panel.
6. Footer with a concise localprocessing note and a control to switch to Privacy.

Use the specified dark design system consistently:

 Background: pure black #000000.
 Header canvas: #09090f transitioning into black only.
 Primary foreground: #f5f5f7.
 Secondary foreground should use controlled opacity rather than unrelated gray colors.
 Brand and interaction accent: pure blue #0000ff.
 Gallery or footeraction tint: rgba(246, 255, 249, 0.72).
 Use 16px rounded cards and inputs.
 Use 18px rounded output or message areas.
 Use 23px rounded pill controls.
 Use 50% rounded icononly buttons.
 Use subtle white separators with rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.16).
 Keep visual density compact but readable with the supplied spacing tokens.
 Use only inline SVGs for the product mark, navigationadjacent marks, copy action, swap action, success state, and any other icons.

Make the conversion card responsive:

 Use a twocolumn input/output grid at widths where both panels remain readable.
 Collapse to one column before either panel becomes too narrow.
 Keep the primary action, clear, swap, and copy controls reachable without horizontal scrolling.
 Preserve a predictable reading order in both layouts.
 Ensure textareas have sufficient minimum height for multiline content.
 Do not hide essential labels or status content at small screen sizes.

Provide the final output as complete code blocks for:

1. server.js
2. index.html

Include only the executable code and minimal required setup instructions after the code blocks.
